headline: Omnicorp Quarterly Report Lists Revenue Source as 'Services Rendered,' Offers No Further Detail
subheadline: Shareholders question $84.7 million in unspecified income; CEO responds: 'You wouldn't understand the services'
summary: Omnicorp Holdings' latest quarterly report has baffled financial analysts with vague revenue categories and unexplained expenditures.
content:
Omnicorp Holdings released its Q3 earnings report last week, and financial analysts are more confused than ever about how the company actually makes money.

The report lists total revenue of $84.7 million, a 4.7% increase from the previous quarter. But the breakdown of revenue sources reads more like a riddle than a financial document.

- **Real Estate Holdings**: $12.3 million (the Hartwell Building and 46 other properties)
- **Consumer Electronics**: $8.1 million (OmniLock, OmniView, OmniListen devices)
- **Services Rendered**: $47.0 million
- **Continuity Maintenance**: $17.3 million

When shareholders asked CEO Victoria Chen to clarify "Services Rendered," she smiled.

"We render services," Chen said. "Services are rendered. The clients who receive these services know what they are. You are not those clients."

"Continuity Maintenance" proved equally opaque. Chen described it only as "ensuring things remain as they should be" and "preventing discontinuities."

"Think of it like... keeping a song playing," she said. "Someone has to make sure the music doesn't stop. That's expensive work. Important work. You're welcome."

The expenditure section raised additional questions. Notable line items included:

- **Geometric Surveys**: $4.7 million
- **Temporal Calibration**: $847,000
- **Floor Maintenance (Unspecified)**: $2.1 million
- **Reflection Quality Assurance**: $313,000

Shareholder activist Marcus Reed demanded specifics. "What floor requires $2.1 million in maintenance? Which floor?"

"An important one," Chen replied.

"Is it Floor 13?" Reed pressed.

"There is no Floor 13," Chen said, still smiling. "The building goes 12, 14. Like most buildings that age. Next question."

Despite the opacity, Omnicorp stock rose 8.47% following the earnings call. Analyst Patricia Womack of TechDaily admitted she couldn't explain investor confidence.

"The numbers don't add up in any traditional sense," Womack said. "But they add up in some sense, clearly. Omnicorp has never missed a dividend. They've never had a down quarter. They've been profitable every single quarter since their founding in... actually, I'm not sure when they were founded. The records are unclear."

Omnicorp Holdings was incorporated in the state in 1923. The same year the Hartwell Building was constructed. The same year the building's architect died under mysterious circumstances.

When asked if there was a connection, Victoria Chen ended the earnings call 47 minutes early.
author: Jerome Wu, Business Reporter
